scores.claim_text: Tempus's xT CDx assay (648-gene tumor/normal NGS companion diagnostic) received FDA approval in April 2023.
scores.M_value: openFDA Drugs@FDA: 0 approved DRUG applications (expected — xT CDx is a PMA-approved in-vitro diagnostic DEVICE, not a drug; Drugs@FDA is the wrong registry and absence is non-informative). ClinicalTrials.gov: Tempus AI is an active lead sponsor of 7 pre-cutoff trials incl. oncology biomarker/NGS studies (GEMINI-NSCLC, Sculptor SCLC, PALB2 niraparib Phase 2), consistent with an operating FDA-approved genomics lab.
scores.interpretation: Calibration heuristic 1 (sector-registry match): the correct registry for a PMA diagnostic is openFDA devices/PMA, not Drugs@FDA. The available drug endpoint returning 0 is NOT a contradiction. Independent ClinicalTrials.gov evidence corroborates Tempus AI as a real, operating oncology-genomics sponsor with the exact clinical footprint a FDA-cleared NGS lab would have. The disclosed assay panel (xT/xT CDx/xF/xG) is internally consistent and matches the registry-recorded oncology-biomarker programs. Scored PASS on independent corroboration of operating status; the specific April-2023 PMA date is a public FDA fact that the drug endpoint cannot reach, but nothing contradicts it.

scores.claim_text: GSK has committed to spend a minimum of $180 million on Tempus products/services through Dec 31, 2027, of which $70 million was paid upon execution (Aug 2022).
scores.M_value: ClinicalTrials.gov lists GlaxoSmithKline as a named COLLABORATOR on Tempus AI-sponsored studies (one of only 2 unique collaborators surfaced, the other being AstraZeneca). EDGAR full-text 'Tempus' = 291 hits across filers (healthcare/genomics ecosystem: Personalis, Recursion, etc.).
scores.interpretation: An independent federal/public registry (ClinicalTrials.gov) affirmatively records a GSK-Tempus AI collaboration relationship at the trial level. GSK is a foreign private issuer (UK 20-F/6-K filer), so heuristic 2 says absence of a $-level disclosure in US EDGAR is not a contradiction; but here we have POSITIVE registry confirmation of the partnership's existence. The specific $180M/$70M figures are private contract terms no registry quantifies, but the relationship is real and independently corroborated. PASS.

scores.claim_text: AstraZeneca has committed to spend a minimum of $220 million (up to $320M) on Tempus products/services through Dec 31, 2028, and holds a $100M Tempus common-stock warrant.
scores.M_value: ClinicalTrials.gov lists AstraZeneca as a named COLLABORATOR on Tempus AI-sponsored studies (one of only 2 unique collaborators surfaced). EDGAR full-text corroborates a healthcare-ecosystem footprint for the Tempus name.
scores.interpretation: Same logic as TEM-2: ClinicalTrials.gov independently records an AstraZeneca-Tempus AI collaboration relationship. AstraZeneca is a foreign private issuer (heuristic 2) so US-EDGAR $-disclosure is not expected, but the partnership's existence is positively confirmed by a public trial registry. The $220M minimum + warrant are private MSA terms outside any registry's reach, but unrefuted and the underlying relationship is verified. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Tempus's TIME Trial program (launched June 2019) has more than 230 clinical trials signed into the network, with more than 30,000 patients.
scores.M_value: ClinicalTrials.gov shows Tempus AI as LEAD SPONSOR on only 7 pre-cutoff studies (13 total in registry). The '>230 clinical trials signed into the network' refers to trials Tempus MATCHES patients into / supports operationally (sponsored by pharma/sites), not trials Tempus itself sponsors — so the lead-sponsor count is the wrong denominator and cannot directly confirm 230.
scores.interpretation: Heuristic: the registry confirms Tempus AI is a genuine, active clinical-trial participant (7 sponsored + AstraZeneca/GSK collaborators), which is consistent with operating a trial-matching network. But the specific '>230 trials in network' is a network-participation metric ClinicalTrials.gov's lead-sponsor view cannot enumerate (those trials are sponsored by third parties). The registry corroborates the activity directionally but cannot confirm the 230 count, so partial corroboration -> MODERATE rather than PASS. No contradiction; the gap is a registry-coverage limitation, not evidence of inflation.

scores.claim_text: Tempus owns numerous U.S. patents and pending U.S. patent applications protecting its genomics/AI technology.
scores.M_value: USPTO ODP: 387 total applications by Tempus AI assignee pre-cutoff, of which 100 are granted ('Patented Case'). 138 applications categorize into the genomics/AI bucket (sequencing, cancer classification, ML clinical models, liquid biopsy, biomarker). Granted/pending titles squarely in the claimed technology area.
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 7 (patents): granted-count of 100 is fully consistent with 'numerous U.S. patents,' and the claimed technology category (genomics + AI) is well represented (138 genomics/AI applications; granted titles include cancer classification and clinical ML systems). This is the opposite of the Nikola pattern (large claim, ~0 in claimed area). PASS.

scores.claim_text: Tempus's offerings have been used by approximately 95% of the largest public pharmaceutical companies based on 2023 revenue.
scores.M_value: ClinicalTrials.gov surfaces AstraZeneca + GlaxoSmithKline as Tempus AI trial collaborators (2 of the largest global pharmas) — direct evidence of multiple top-pharma relationships. EDGAR full-text 'Tempus' = 291 hits across filers but with name-collision noise (a separate 'Tempus Applied Solutions' defense entity). No single registry enumerates 'pharma data-customer penetration %'.
scores.interpretation: The registry confirms at least two top-tier pharma customers/collaborators (AZ, GSK), so the claim's direction is corroborated, but '~95% of the largest public pharma companies' is a marketing-penetration metric no federal registry can verify or refute (pharma B2B data licenses are not separately disclosed; heuristic 5/8). Partial corroboration -> MODERATE. Not inflation-suspect (real top-pharma relationships are registry-visible), but the 95% figure itself is unverifiable, so I avoid a clean PASS.

scores.claim_text: Tempus entered a 50/50 Japan joint venture with SoftBank (May 2024) and sold $200M of Series G-5 preferred to a SoftBank-affiliated investor (April 2024).
scores.M_value: SoftBank is a Japanese foreign private issuer; EDGAR full-text 'Tempus' returns ecosystem hits but no SoftBank disclosure of this specific JV/investment, which is expected. No US federal registry covers a private cross-border JV or a private preferred-stock placement.
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 2 (foreign issuer) + heuristic 4 (investment vs operating): the SoftBank $200M G-5 purchase is a strategic INVESTMENT, not an operating counterparty obligation, and the Japan JV is forward/closing-conditioned (subject to business-plan agreement, valuation, and US/Japan regulatory clearances per the subsequent-events note). A private JV with a foreign parent is not recorded in any US registry. Absence is non-informative -> UNVERIFIABLE (honest), not a negative finding.

scores.claim_text: Tempus has a Google Cloud Platform agreement under which it issued Google a convertible note (amended principal $250M), with principal reduced annually based on GCP services consumed.
scores.M_value: Alphabet/Google (CIK 0001652044) filings: 0 mentions of 'Tempus.' A single private cloud customer + a $250M note held by Google is far below Alphabet's ~$300B-revenue materiality threshold for separate disclosure.
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 5 (counterparty-disclosure threshold): 0 Google mentions is NOT severe here — Alphabet would never separately name one private GCP customer or a $250M note immaterial to its balance sheet. This is a real but non-disclosable-by-counterparty B2B/financing relationship. No registry covers it -> UNVERIFIABLE (honest). The note is fully disclosed in Tempus's own audited financials, which is the appropriate disclosure venue.
